title: Final pre-owner-test pass: File Intelligence sidecar, trader series identity, run provenance
body:
Final integration pass on top of PR #58 (`night/v7-convergence-20260908` @ `45027d3`). Four goals only: integrate AI File Sorter as a governed capability, close the two remaining repository integrity gaps, harden, and freeze one SHA for owner testing. No new architecture, no Epoch, no V7/V8 systems.

**FINAL_CODE_SHA = `a1e633cb3c961302a74bac63da51be16fd08c53b`** — code frozen here; only documentation moves after it. Current head `e5ccd54` is docs-only above it.

> The freeze moved twice, and both moves are recorded rather than smoothed over. `cf020da → 9bea81a`: auditing the hostile matrix found a real gap (a swapped sidecar binary was undetectable). `9bea81a → a1e633c`: Command Center CI had **never completed** on this branch — see "Route leak" below. Freezing with a known hole and calling it frozen would have been the wrong trade both times.

## Starting truth, verified before touching code

| | |
| --- | --- |
| PR58 head | `45027d3e9aef554407a0a9ff07fb8678d1b849f3` — re-checked at the end, unmoved |
| Frozen runtime code before this pass | `22ae555bc317c45abc925f70566fea90cd495692` — confirmed: the only commits after it on that line touch `docs/final/FINAL_OWNER_TEST_CANDIDATE_20260908.md` and nothing else |
| Default branch | `2a7d3a2dd7eca278322a34afa9ca3c69a4ee3c1d` — **not** merged in |
| Upstream AI File Sorter | `4dc374df69b5e63d5354e121097d92e25bbd32da` — confirmed with `git ls-remote`, then cloned and read at that SHA |

PR59 is not merged, Token Shunt and Visual V3 stay spec-only, and nothing in the preserve list (AT-01, AT-03, Video CFR, approval CAS, policy DENY monotonicity, B4/B5, World State, OpenHands isolation, SSRF, Stop/Pause precedence…) was reopened.

## 1. Trader metric-series identity

The module's first documented rule was "never compare absolute CVD/OI values across different providers/settings". It lived only in the docstring: `Snapshot` carried `source`/`instrument`/`timestamp` and `classify_regime` read none of them, so a Binance perp CVD and a Bybit CVD were subtracted as happily as two rows from one feed.

Adds immutable `SeriesId` descriptors (provider, instrument, market, aggregation, normalization, version) per metric and proves compatibility before any subtraction. Refuses with a named reason on source mismatch, instrument mismatch, CVD series mismatch, OI series mismatch, missing or incomplete identity, and a previous timestamp not strictly before the current one.

Missing identity is refused rather than treated as a match — that is the case this exists for, since two rows both defaulting to `"unknown"` compared equal as strings. On refusal all three directions return UNKNOWN, not just the regime. A metric that is *absent* still needs no identity. ANALYSIS_ONLY is unchanged.

## 2. Immutable run provenance

`task_runs` remembered one thing about who executed a run: `model_alias`. Everything else lived in `agents` — mutable, with `ON DELETE SET NULL`. Editing an agent rewrote the past; deleting one erased it.

Provenance is captured at run start in `_run()` and stored on the run: agent identity and a content-addressed revision, `system_prompt_sha256`, model and fallback identities, allowed-tools/permissions/policy digests, privacy mode, budget identity, repository SHA. Immutability is enforced by a **database trigger**; it permits the first write and an idempotent repeat, and refuses everything else including NULL-ing. No hidden reasoning, no plaintext secrets, and **no backfill**: pre-existing runs report `NOT_CAPTURED`.

## 3. File Intelligence — governed AI File Sorter sidecar

**Licence boundary.** No AGPL C++ vendored. `integrations/ai-file-sorter/` holds the manifest and NOTICE with the verified pin and AGPL-3.0-or-later.

**Contract.** The documented headless CLI, not GUI automation. `argv` is a list built from enums and scope-checked paths — no shell string. Analysis is `--review-only` with no parameter to make it otherwise. All four upstream spellings of auto-apply, plus `=value` forms, are rejected in the *built* argv. Apply takes neither path nor operation.

**Scope.** Repositories (any nested `.git`), Bossman state, secrets directories, system roots and workspaces are denied by default. Repository *mutation* has no opt-in at all.

**Evidence.** Source identity is captured at **review**, so a same-size, restored-mtime replacement is caught. Apply derives a filtered plan of approved entries only — otherwise approving 5 of 20 files would apply 20. After apply Bossman re-reads the filesystem itself; disagreement is `VERIFICATION_FAILED`, never `COMPLETED`. The sidecar binary is re-hashed immediately before dispatch and refused on mismatch.

**Privacy fails closed.** `LLMChoice::Custom`/`Unset` are UNKNOWN and refused even with owner approval; upstream's `is_remote_choice()` would have counted `Custom` as local.

**Honest gaps.** `UNDO_HEADLESS=UNAVAILABLE`; `VERSION_UNVERIFIED` for the owner's build.

Flag `file_intelligence_v1` is **OFF by default**, no tick loop, nothing created at startup. Measured marginal import cost **3.9 ms**.

## 4. Route leak — why Command Center CI had never completed here

Both Command Center CI runs on `76b9585` were killed at the workflow's 30-minute job limit. The base branch finishes the same suite in ~22–26 minutes; locally it took 18 minutes before File Intelligence and **58 minutes** after.

The feature module built its action routes inside `attach(svc)`, called from `setup()` — appending six routes to the **shared module-level router on every app start**. Measured: 1 → 7 → 13 → 19 across three starts. Production starts once; a test process starts the app hundreds of times, so `include_router` copied everything accumulated (quadratic) and every request matched linearly against every copy.

`a1e633c` declares the routes once at module level, reading `request.app.state.svc` exactly as `governor.py` does. Two regressions guard it (route count stable across four app starts; all seven endpoints non-404 in a fresh interpreter).

**Proven.** Locally the suite is back to **18:08** (2897 passed, 0 failed). In CI: both Command Center runs on `a1e633c` concluded `success`, and on `e5ccd54` (identical code) the push-run concluded `success` with py3.11 at 26:16, py3.12 at 23:33, py3.14 at 19:24.

Withdrawn after measurement: an intermediate hypothesis that the endpoints were unreachable in a fresh production process. They were reachable (200).

## 5. AP-001 and STOP_GRACE

**AP-001**: a token planted outside every authorized root is read through four escape shapes; each is refused *and* the token stays out of the model-visible result; a negative control proves the same token *is* readable in scope. Absolute-read-from-legitimate-cwd is `NOT_TESTED_ON_THIS_HOST`.

**STOP_GRACE**: reproduced with a loop holding a real DB connection past the 2 s window; four runs show no product violation. Left at 2 s. `HOST_DEPENDENT_OWNER_ACCEPTANCE`.

## Results on the frozen SHA `a1e633c`

Every local row was measured on `a1e633c`, one suite at a time, with HEAD verified identical at start and end. The CI column covers `a1e633c` and the docs-only `e5ccd54` (identical code) and is ticked only where a run actually reached a conclusion.

| suite | local | CI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| root | 1192 passed | ✅ py3.12 both heads · py3.11: runner-noise fail on `a1e633c`, ✅ on `e5ccd54` |
| Bossman Core | 3012 passed, 41 skipped | ✅ both heads |
| Command Center | 2897 passed, 19 skipped — **18:08** | ✅ `a1e633c` ×2 · `e5ccd54` push-run ✅ · PR-run py3.11 **hit 30-min cap** (see below) |
| Editors (real browser) | 5 passed | ✅ |
| Fable media preflight / Fleet / Video Studio+Web | 3 / 88 / 335 passed, 11 skipped | ✅ |
| ASTRA (core + CC) | 98 + 24 passed | ✅ |
| Solana safety | 30 passed | ✅ |
| internal benchmark | 17 passed | ✅ |
| new this pass | 161 passed, 3 skipped | — |
| scorecard · skips registry · compileall · secret scan · whitespace | PASS | ✅ |

**Command Center `pytest (py3.11)`, PR-run on `e5ccd54`: 30 min 17 s → job timeout.** Identical code passed py3.11 in 26:16 in the same wave; the base branch's own py3.11 runs **25:37**, so headroom under the 30-minute cap was ~4 min before this PR and the runner swing here exceeded it. This PR adds ~40 s to that job. **Proposed, not pushed:** raise `timeout-minutes` for the Command Center test job from 30 to 45 (or split the matrix) — CI configuration is the owner's call during a code freeze. Full analysis in the last comment.

**`root pytest + hygiene (py3.11)`** failed once on `a1e633c` on a V5 `ObjectiveStore` latency test the diff cannot reach, with the test's own host-floor control showing the runner stalled; it passed on `e5ccd54` (identical code). Threshold untouched.

Two corrections stated rather than quietly fixed: an earlier Core run showed 11 benchmark failures because I committed while it ran (the engine correctly refused to bind a report to a moved HEAD — re-run motionless: 3012/0); and an earlier revision of this description ticked Command Center CI before any run had actually concluded.

## Deliberately NOT claimed

`WINDOWS_OWNER`, `LOCAL_MODEL`, `AIFS_REAL_BINARY`, `AIFS_REAL_LOCAL_MODEL`, real OpenHands/OpenRouter/GLM, N4/N5/N6/N8, canary/rollback and soak are **NOT_RUN** — they need the owner's machine.

`INTELLIGENCE_RETENTION = INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`. `measured intelligence retention` is red here and **red on the base**, and must stay red: every route to green fabricates evidence.

Owner-test document: `docs/final/OWNER_TEST_20260908_FILE_INTELLIGENCE.md`.

title: Final audit closure 2026-09-08: completion truth (P0), OpenHands evidence (P1), bounded recovery/streaming/resources (P2), Web Designer & Coding owner paths
body:
## Purpose

Convergence of all current audits (Astra/Codex latest breaker `d33288f`, owner manual audit `1531b16`, independent total audit `1da5b57`, historical audit branches, owner sessions `5893ffba6724` / `2fdf5629d0d9`) on the canonical night head `45027d3`. Every finding was reproduced on `45027d3` before any code changed; every fix carries a negative and a positive control.

BASE_SHA `45027d3e9aef554407a0a9ff07fb8678d1b849f3` · FIX_SHA (all code) `69df482c6ab94f04b17715d9e2ceb4a695d20590` · the same commit is pushed as `freeze/final-audit-closure-20260908`.

## P0 — completion truth (owner tasks 22/44/45, reproduced 7/10 on HEAD)
- `finalize`: an empty answer with no verified declared effect and no executed effectful tool call is `EMPTY_RESULT` → `failed`, never `completed`. Conversational answers still complete; effect tasks still complete on verified effect.
- A human challenge in the browser (CAPTCHA, anti-bot) is a **state**: `verification.BLOCKED` → task `paused` with `reason_code=WAITING_FOR_OWNER_CHALLENGE`; browser-session Resume continues the same run exactly once; stale/consumed Resume resurrects nothing. The model's "complete the CAPTCHA and press Resume" prose also parks the task.
- `url_contains=youtube.com` no longer verifies a content goal: play/watch goals derive `youtube.com/watch`; `higgsfield` is a known domain; «в новом текстовом документе» is a file obligation.

## P1 — OpenHands evidence independence (Astra F1, 2/2)
Change set derived from the working tree against HEAD's tree (blob hashes); the index has no say. `assume-unchanged`/`skip-worktree` → refusal; edited `.gitignore`/`.git/info/exclude` disable ignore filtering; git's view may add paths but never hide one.

## P2
- Recovery ladder (F6): spent rungs persist across failure classes; global budget `max_retries + 2`; stopped tasks are not re-queued by a late failure.
- Streaming (F2/F3): `max_chunks` bounds upstream reads; new `completion` field (complete/capped/partial/malformed/timeout/silent/rate_limited/provider_error); `ok` requires a whole answer.
- Reality route (F5): NaN/inf/negative memory → 422 before coercion.
- Sandbox cleanup (F4): honest result, bounded retry, read-only handling, never outside the sandbox root or inside the source repo.
- Action contract negation (F7): only the negated span is removed; mixed sentences keep the requested action (EN+RU).

## UX
- Web Designer: second Apply is idempotent (frame re-describes the selected element; reproduced in real Chromium on HEAD first); model selector backed by the canonical registry with health, server default by health rank instead of `models[0]`.
- Coding: «Новая задача агенту» → the single existing OpenHands runtime (readiness, running/blocked/failed/completed, diff, evidence, sandbox cleanup state; no push/merge/deploy by construction). `bossman doctor` reports OpenHands readiness.

## Docs
`docs/final_closure/MASTER_FINDINGS.md` (33 rows), `OWNER_SESSION_CLUSTERING.md` (21 clusters over 14 614 records), `OWNER_BREAKER_SETUP.md` (evening flow + breaker corpus B1–B10). The exact-SHA suite report follows once the local full runs and CI finish.

## Not done / external
- Intelligence Preservation still requires a genuine current same-model measurement → EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED; the gate was not weakened.
- Live OpenRouter/GLM, real OpenHands SDK run, Windows file locks, Higgsfield authenticated generation remain owner-live.

title: feat: AI streamer media factory — Higgsfield browser generation wired into the Social Farm runtime
body:
Started as the design pack plus typed contracts. It now also contains the implementation those contracts were written for, wired into the browser runtime that already existed rather than beside it.

## What changed since the contracts

**The adapter goes through the account session, not past it.** The first version drove a raw `DomPort` — a port that can click and read and nothing else. It does not know whose account is in the context, keeps no journal, counts no failures and cannot call the owner. An adapter built on it does not defeat those protections; it never meets them. Every step now runs through `AccountBrowserSession`, so identity is verified before the first action, a CAPTCHA or re-login moves the session to `TAKEOVER_REQUIRED` and the job to `HUMAN_CHALLENGE`/`NEEDS_OWNER_AUTH`, the target fingerprint is retaken immediately before each click, every lifecycle event lands in the redacted audit, and three deterministic failures on one selector pack version park the capability.

**A click is not proof of submission.** Two independent page observations are required, and the count is a module constant rather than configuration, because a configurable minimum can be set to zero. Fewer signals stop the job and do *not* resubmit it: an unobserved click is not "it failed", it is "unknown", and retrying an unknown spends the owner's credits twice.

**A downloaded file becomes a result only after it is measured.** Quarantine → probe → promote into the approved workspace, under a name built from the job id and the *measured* extension, so an error page named `scene.mp4` is rejected precisely because it is named `scene.mp4`. Refusals are separated by what the owner should do next, and the file is kept beside a note rather than deleted.

**A restart must not generate the same clip twice.** The submission receipt is durable and written before the wait; a job is led by one worker at a time through a lease with an expiry, over an `O_EXCL` file lock; resume enters at the point the job actually reached. Polling backs off and cannot be configured to shrink.

**The router stops believing numbers nobody measured.** An observation is a value plus its source and age, and an unmeasured or stale fact closes a route rather than opening one — which is the OOM negative control. Quality became a gate rather than a score term, so the browser path is reached by a scene asking for it instead of winning every comparison.

**Persona canon is versioned and partly locked**, and QA observations never rewrite it. Prompts are assembled by name from a closed list, with no parameter through which anything else could be passed.

**OpenHands repairs selectors and cannot disable them.** The drift packet is built by subtraction — no markup, no field values, no element refs, no query string — and refuses to travel at all if something key-shaped is found in it. Its mission may touch the selector pack, the adapter and tests; challenge detection, isolation, secret redaction, the capability ledger and the whole control plane are protected paths. Diffs that skip a test, delete an assertion, swallow every exception or click by coordinates are inadmissible.

**Six unattended hours run on a virtual clock**, deterministically, with `deadlock_count = 0` as a hard requirement and a negative control that forces the counter up. A human challenge pauses one lane; the other two keep producing.

## Also in here

Three latent bugs in the contracts as merged: `UI_CHANGED` and `RATE_LIMITED` had no edge out of `AUTH_CHECK` and collapsed into `FAILED`, which the worker retries — sending attempts back into the same changed interface and the same rate limit; `POLICY_BLOCKED` and `UI_CHANGED` had no edge out of `WAITING_PROVIDER`, so the worker's own handler for them raised mid-flight. `plan()` never told the capability ledger about a missing target, so demotion on a vanished control never fired at all.

`apps/social-farm` had **no CI job of any kind** — 500-odd tests existed only on whoever ran them by hand. There is a workflow now, with Chromium and ffmpeg installed so the browser and media tests run instead of skipping.

## What this does not claim

Repository tests are not live acceptance and nothing here converts one into the other. There is no Higgsfield account in this environment; the selector pack is version `0.1.0-unverified` because its strategies were written against a documented UI rather than an observed one; no file in these tests came from Higgsfield; six virtual hours are not six real ones. A capability proven on a fixture stays `EXPERIMENTAL` by construction, and no test in this repository can promote it.

`docs/ai_streamer/IMPLEMENTATION_MAP_20260908.md` maps each design requirement onto the code and test that answers it, and lists exactly what still needs the owner's machine.

title: V7 night convergence: review deadlock, approval storm, token loops, B2–B5, OpenHands, golden replay, V7 reality core, UX
body:
Autonomous convergence run against `docs/night/NIGHT_V7_CONVERGENCE_MASTER_20260908.md`, plus the multi-model V7 audit corpus pinned in `docs/night/V7_MULTIMODEL_AUDIT_REFERENCES_20260908.md`. **28 commits, 109 files, +14 812/−339.**

Every number below was produced by running the thing and counting what happened. `cd bossman-core && python -m bossman.v7.nightly_run --objectives all` reproduces all of it and reports **10/10 objectives PASS** in ~123s. Final report: `docs/night/NIGHT_V7_CONVERGENCE_FINAL_REPORT_20260908.md`.

## P0 — review/escalation deadlock (INV-RD-1)

A task in `waiting_approval` could outlive every decision object it waited for. The 202-event acceptance corpus hit this four times (`pending_approvals: 0`, checkpoint note `review_escalated`, retry refused `TASK_STATE_CONFLICT`); `/stop` was the only escape. Three paths produced it: a REJECTED escalation nobody settled, an APPROVED escalation renamed before `finalize_override` ran so its refusal burned the only live decision, and any other path whose approval was decided or deleted without releasing the task.

`bcc/review_escalation.py` adds the terminating half of the state machine — `live_decision` names what can still act, `advance` re-asks within a bounded budget or fails with the honest reason, `reconcile` sweeps what the known paths miss (unconditionally, every 10s tick). No gate is weakened: `finalize_override` still demands fresh verification and still refuses, and nothing here can write `completed`.

Also fixes a root cause behind two of the four: a hostname inside a URL matched the filename regex, so a task mentioning `https://example.com` was handed a `file:example.com` obligation it could never satisfy.

**Measured: 4 deadlocks reproduced, 0 survive the sweep, review_deadlock_rate 0.0.**

The same failure existed on the core side and is fixed too: `approvals.wait()` held a task for up to 24 hours while asking the owner exactly *once*, at creation. A lost notification meant nobody was ever asked again. It now re-asks at 1m/5m/15m/1h/6h/12h, emits `approval.waiting`, survives a broken notification channel without releasing the wait, and backs off 0.5s→15s instead of 43 200 queries a day. The window stays a full day — narrowing it silently would take away the owner's right to decide later.

And the sweep that enforces all this is now *watchable*: feature tick loops appear on `/api/health` under the same rules as the worker and scheduler, where only a successful pass advances the clock. A loop that died or threw on every pass used to look identical to a working one.

## Approval storm

161 confirmations in one session, ~121 of them for a documentation edit. Added dedup of identical pending questions, suppression of already-refused calls, owner-granted scoped leases (tool + effect class + mode + agent + task, mandatory expiry and use count, instant revocation) and a per-task approval budget that stops the task rather than auto-approving.

**Measured: a documentation edit costs 2 approvals (read, then write) or 1 (single write), against the corpus's 60.** The second question is correct and is reported as such: a read lease must not cover a write, which is the master's own "unless policy requires more for a specific real effect". Asking for the *same* effect twice still fails the benchmark.

## Token / loop guardrails

1 282 044 tokens and $4.04 for a two-line doc fix. Added token and cost ceilings, an identical-call loop guard, a stalled-context guard, and the §8 metric block at `GET /api/tasks/{id}/efficiency`. A breach fails the run with a named reason — it never trims context, downgrades the model, or marks work complete.

**Measured: 1 840 and 920 tokens for the two doc-edit shapes, against the corpus's 1 295 189. Both completed.**

## B3 — Apps control

All nine apps refused start/stop with 409 because control could only be enabled by editing the environment and restarting. Now a persistent owner policy that takes effect immediately and survives restart, with policy refusal split from state conflict (403 `APPS_CONTROL_DISABLED` vs 409). Default stays closed; a deployment lock can pin it beyond the API's reach.

## B4 — unified streaming

One canonical SSE parser (`bcc/streaming.py`) behind every OpenAI-compatible variant — `delta.content`, `delta.reasoning`, `delta.reasoning_content`, content arrays, tool calls, `message.content` — with `SUPPORTED / DEGRADED / FAILED / PROVIDER_FAILED` told apart instead of collapsed. GLM 5.3 streams again.

## B5 — model health

`check_model` recorded a pass for a model that answered nothing. Health is now classified from the answer, not the HTTP status: `HEALTHY / SILENT / MALFORMED / THROTTLED / UNAUTHORIZED / PROVIDER_DOWN / TIMEOUT / UNMEASURED`, with cooldowns and ranked fallback. A model that returns silence raises `ProviderError(kind="empty_response")` rather than being counted well.

## B2 — secure local cloud-QA relay

Cloud QA could not test Video Studio, Web Designer or Apps at all: the browser tool refuses loopback URLs. The relay is a signed job contract (HMAC-SHA256, single-use nonces, TTL, capability allowlist, sanitized and size-capped evidence, owner kill switch, audit log) so a cloud agent can drive the real local system without a public URL.

**Measured: 4/4 systems answered, 0 manual interventions, and every negative control held — replayed job, forged signature, unlisted capability and post-kill-switch job all refused.**

## OpenHands — real execution

The stub is gone. `openhands-sdk` 1.44.1 is installed and the tests spawn the real sidecar, which builds a real `Agent`/`Conversation` and dispatches the SDK's real `file_editor` and `terminal` tools against a real git worktree. Running it for real exposed three defects that no mock would have: the SDK's visualizer wrote to stdout and corrupted the JSON protocol, new files never appeared in the derived evidence diff, and worktree creation failed whenever `origin/<base>` did not exist. All three fixed; 10 tests, none vacuous — they skip loudly if the SDK is absent.

The one substitution is the model's weights: a scripted local OpenAI-compatible endpoint stands in, because no LLM provider credential exists in this environment (a keyless probe of the configured endpoint returns 401). That boundary is stated, not papered over.

## Golden trace replay

The 202-event corpus is now a regression rather than a souvenir: `bcc/golden_trace.py` extracts each recorded pathology (deadlocks, approval storm, token burn, provider-down, owner interventions, repeated reviews, cloud-routed successes) and 18 tests assert the fixed system no longer reproduces them.

## V7 reality core, and the multi-model audit corpus

`bcc/reality/` — intent compiler (Mission IR, digest-bound), observation adapters that report `available: false` with a reason rather than a zero, strategy generation with evidence *bands* instead of invented decimals, a recovery ladder, and shadow telemetry recording what the shadow router recommended versus what production did. Advisory by construction: there is deliberately no endpoint that executes, applies or promotes anything.

The eight pinned V7 audit branches were then read at their exact SHAs (all matched) and classified in `docs/v7/MULTIMODEL_AUDIT_SYNTHESIS_20260908.md`: 12 recommendations already implemented and mapped to the file that implements them, 4 stale (two contradicting the corpus's own rules), 2 model-vs-model disagreements resolved rather than averaged, 3 real gaps closed, 5 recorded as still-valid and deliberately unbuilt with reasons.

The three gaps, closed here:

1. **The World State Graph had no runtime path.** The storage contract existed, the adapters existed, `to_world_facts()` shaped one for the other — and nothing ingested them, so the graph was empty between requests and freshness described nothing. `bcc/reality/world.py` keeps one projection per process, refreshes it on a 60s tick (deliberately slower than the facts' own validity, so the graph can actually go STALE), and serves it read-only at `GET /reality/world`. A value appears only under a FRESH status, and no route writes a fact — asserted, not intended.
2. **Two observers disagreeing was settled by recency** — the failure the corpus names first for this layer ("the World State Graph becomes a stale cache treated as truth"). Facts are now kept per source; while two fresh readings disagree the read is `CONTESTED` and returns UNKNOWN. Strictly a tightening: a read that was FRESH can become CONTESTED, nothing that was UNKNOWN becomes known. `require_fresh()` makes the effect-boundary rule callable rather than conventional.
3. **Generation-aware single-flight** on the observation pass, per the charter: the tick and a request no longer each shell out to git for the same answer.

## UX consolidation

Two flat sections (~20 entries, Video Studio next to "Развилки") became six named spaces. 13 browser tests check the opposite of what a tidy-up usually breaks: every route still exists, still renders, and is still reachable — including the ones deliberately hidden from the menu.

## Testing — all on one frozen head

| suite | result |
| --- | --- |
| bossman-core | 2 952 passed, 31 skipped, 0 failed |
| Command Center | 2 577 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed |
| root | 1 163 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed |
| CI on `3561f3b` | 24 check runs — 23 success, 1 skipped |
| secret scan | PASS |

Also fixed along the way, both pre-existing and both outside this run's diff: root-ci's whitespace gate (red on `main` and every branch cut from it) and a browser test that asserted `events == 1` while a 30-second background poller could fire its own 401 into the same window.

## Known, and not this PR's to decide

**This branch conflicts with `main`** in `bossman-core/bossman/{cli.py,gateway/app.py,gateway/backends.py}`. The conflict predates this run — the branch base already conflicted, and 164 of the branch's commits precede these 28. `main` rewrote the gateway for 8 providers while the branch added a `CircuitOpenError` circuit breaker to the same functions; picking either side loses behavior, and `main`'s own root-ci is red with `ImportError: cannot import name 'CircuitOpenError'`, so which gateway ships is an open question rather than a mechanical merge. Full history in the thread below.

*(The latency-acceptance flake noted in the earlier revision of this description is resolved: it was runner noise, it is green on the current head, and the only change made was to publish `floor_over_limit` beside the verdict — which decides nothing, asserted directly.)*

title: build: downloadable local bundle (3.2 MB) — and the wheel that shipped no UI
body:
Gives the owner a way to download **only what a machine needs to run Bossman** — 3.2 MB instead of the whole repository — and fixes the packaging defect that building it exposed.

## The defect (the more valuable half)

**The Command Center wheel ships no interface at all.**

- `[tool.setuptools.packages.find] include = ["bcc*"]` captures the package; `command-center/ui` sits *beside* it and is excluded.
- The installed server resolves `ui_dir` as `ROOT / "ui"`, where `ROOT = PKG_DIR.parent`. Under a wheel that is `site-packages`, which has no `ui`.
- `api.py:520` mounts static files only `if settings.ui_dir.is_dir()`.

So a wheel install starts a server, answers the API, and serves **no interface**, without a single error line. Silent degradation, not a crash — which is why it survived this long.

**Fix:** `ui_dir` now honours `BCC_UI_DIR`, matching the idiom its neighbours already use (`BCC_DATA_DIR`, `BCC_HOST`, `BCC_PORT`). The default is unchanged, so running from a source checkout behaves exactly as before. The bundle ships `ui/` beside the wheels and points the variable at it.

## Verification is the point

A directory of files nobody tried to install is not a delivery. The builder creates a clean virtual environment, installs the wheels, imports the packages, checks every declared entry point exists, and asserts the **installed** package resolves the UI and finds `index.html`.

That last check exists because my first version didn't have it: it checked imports and entry points, reported `verified: yes`, and shipped a bundle containing **zero UI files**. Confirming files exist is not confirming the product can find them.

## Two smaller things found while building

- `python -m build` is not universally installed — and an `import build` probe can be satisfied by a stray `build/` directory in the working tree, which is exactly how it fooled me here. Uses `pip wheel` instead.
- Build isolation must stay **on**: Debian's patched setuptools fails with `AttributeError: install_layout`.

## CI

`Local bundle` workflow, manual dispatch or a `v*` tag, builds on **Linux and Windows** and uploads the artifact. Separate runners because "it built on mine" is not "it installs on the owner's".
